summary: R3-NEW-MAJ-001 (safety) closure is REAL: invariant 2's blocked-on-adopter-conflict bullet now explicitly asserts 'PR MUST NOT modify branch-protection-log.md', §5.2 item (2) echoes 'CI script asserts absence of modification per invariant 2', and §6 024B acceptance row requires 'asserts log file was NOT modified'. All three sites are consistent. The bypass surface R3 identified is closed. However, the surface scan finds two new issues: (1) R-024-06 in the risk table was NOT updated by fix-round-3 — it still says only 'verifies the TF reference is present', omitting the new log-file-absence assertion; this is an internal inconsistency that a Codex executor implementing from the risk table alone would implement only half the check (MAJ). (2) The onboarded-operator-bump CI check verifies only that STATUS.md contains the standardised prefix string — it does not require the row to carry any meaningful content (e.g. a Renovate PR URL, an open/in-progress marker, or any field beyond the bare slug). A stub row (just the prefix + adopter slug, no status) passes CI; the Threshold A credit mechanism is then entirely reviewer-dependent with no machine-verifiable signal that a real Renovate cycle occurred. This is the same negative-assertion gap pattern as R3-NEW-MAJ-001 safety: positive evidence is verified (prefix present), but no minimum-content requirement is asserted (MAJ). R4 fixpoint criterion: 0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ — not met.

findings.title: R3-NEW-MAJ-001 (safety) closure verification: log-file-absence assertion for blocked-on-adopter-conflict — CLOSED
findings.evidence: Three plan-doc sites verified as consistent: (a) Invariant 2, blocked-on-adopter-conflict bullet: 'PR MUST NOT modify docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md (no enable-required-check.sh invocation occurred — closing the bypass surface that R3 safety surfaced) AND MUST reference the filed TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF in DISPATCH-NOTE matching the standardised prefix.' (b) §5.2 item (2), blocked-on-adopter-conflict value description: 'the PR MUST NOT modify branch-protection-log.md (CI script asserts absence of modification per invariant 2).' (c) §6 024B acceptance row: 'for blocked-on-adopter-conflict: requires TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference AND asserts log file was NOT modified (closes the R3 safety bypass).' All three sites specify both the positive assertion (TF reference present) and the negative assertion (log file NOT modified). FIX-ROUND-3.md claim matches. The bypass path described in R3-NEW-MAJ-001 — declare blocked-on-adopter-conflict, invoke enable-required-check.sh, commit the log entry, file the TF reference, pass CI — is closed because the CI script now also asserts log-file unmodified.

findings.title: R-024-06 risk-table mitigation NOT updated: omits log-file-absence assertion for blocked-on-adopter-conflict, creating an authoritative implementation reference that specifies only half the CI check
findings.evidence: R-024-06 mitigation in §7 reads: 'The CI invocation-log check (invariant 2 carve-out) skips log-entry assertion for these close-state slices but verifies the TF reference is present.' This text was NOT updated by fix-round-3. Fix-round-3 added the log-file-absence assertion to invariant 2, §5.2, and §6 024B — but not to R-024-06. The risk table is a normative section that Codex executors read when implementing cascade slices; R-024-06 is the canonical description of how T-024-10 is mitigated. A Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh from R-024-06 alone would implement only the TF-reference presence check, omitting the log-file-absence assertion. The inconsistency across the plan-doc's four sites that specify the blocked-on-adopter-conflict CI behaviour (invariant 2, §5.2, §6 024B, and R-024-06) means the fix is incomplete: three of four sites are correct; one authoritative site (the risk table mitigation that Codex executors use) still describes the pre-fix, bypass-vulnerable specification. This is not a nit — the risk table entry is the implementation-guidance anchor for cascade-slice authors and Codex executors, and it currently instructs them to implement a check that was demonstrated (at R3) to be bypassable.
findings.recommendation: Amend R-024-06 mitigation to: 'T-024-10 mitigation: cascade slice CLOSES with status blocked-on-adopter-conflict per invariant 10 (forward TF TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> owned by the slice author; new sub-slice opens on conflict resolution). The CI invocation-log check (invariant 2 carve-out) for these close-state slices: (a) MUST NOT find branch-protection-log.md modified in the PR diff (assert log file unmodified — no enable-required-check.sh invocation occurred); (b) MUST find a TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference in DISPATCH-NOTE matching the standardised prefix. Both assertions are required; either failure causes CI to fail.' This makes R-024-06 consistent with invariant 2, §5.2, and §6 024B.

findings.title: onboarded-operator-bump CI check verifies prefix presence only — stub STATUS.md row (bare prefix, no content) passes CI; Threshold A credit mechanism for operator-bump adopters is entirely reviewer-dependent with no machine-verifiable evidence of a real Renovate cycle
findings.evidence: Invariant 2, onboarded-operator-bump bullet: 'STATUS.md MUST contain a row matching the standardised prefix TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>.' R-024-07: 'the check-invocation-log-entry.sh CI script verifies STATUS.md contains the matching TF row when DISPATCH-NOTE declares cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump.' The CI check is a string-containment check: does STATUS.md contain the string 'TF-024X-renovate-<owner>-<repo>'? A STATUS.md row consisting solely of '| TF-024X-renovate-owner-reponame | | | |' (bare prefix slug, empty status, no Renovate PR URL, no closure evidence) passes this check. The TF row is a STATUS.md markdown row — not a tracked ticket in a system that has open/closed state. 'Closing' the TF at Threshold A time means editing the STATUS.md row to indicate closed; that edit is not independently verified by CI. Threshold A criterion (§8): 'Each onboarded adopter has survived ≥1 SCP minor version-bump cycle propagated cleanly — via Renovate... Adopters who satisfied the per-slice bake via an operator-driven bump (R-024-07 fallback) do NOT count toward Threshold A until a real Renovate cycle has also merged + observed clean.' The 024G reviewer is responsible for verifying the real Renovate cycle occurred. However, the plan-doc specifies no machine-verifiable content requirement for the TF row beyond the prefix string. A malicious or careless author can: (1) declare cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump, (2) add a stub row 'TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>' with no content, (3) pass the CI check, (4) later mark the TF row as closed in STATUS.md without any supporting Renovate PR URL, (5) present the closed row to the 024G reviewer as evidence of Threshold A compliance. The 024G reviewer has no CI backstop and must manually verify the Renovate PR exists on the adopter repo. The plan-doc (R3 scan R3-SCAN-TF-RENOVATE-FILING-VS-CLOSING) assessed this as MIN, noting the real Renovate cycle requirement is independently verifiable by the 024G reviewer. However, R3 assessed that finding before the fix-round-3 pattern was established: fix-round-3's R3-NEW-MAJ-001 safety fix explicitly established the principle that a carve-out skip-the-check clause needs BOTH positive evidence AND absence of contradicting evidence. The same principle applies here: the operator-bump path needs the STATUS.md row to contain minimum meaningful content (at minimum a Renovate PR URL field that is populated before Threshold A credit is claimed) — not just the bare prefix. The R4 scan is the first cycle where this pattern is evaluated against the new fix-round-3 heuristic. The gap is MAJ because: (a) it opens a Threshold A bypass path where an adopter counts toward the gate without a proven automated version-skew-tolerance cycle; (b) the operator-bump vs Renovate distinction is the primary mechanism by which the plan-doc prevents Threshold A from being satisfied via one-off operator actions; (c) a stub TF row with no content requirement undermines this distinction at the only point where CI could enforce it.
findings.recommendation: Amend the onboarded-operator-bump CI check in invariant 2 and R-024-07 to require that the STATUS.md TF row contains a minimum-content field: specifically, the row MUST include a 'Renovate PR:' or equivalent field that is either 'pending' (at onboarded-operator-bump close time) or a resolved GitHub PR URL (at Threshold A credit time). The check-invocation-log-entry.sh script should verify at onboarded-operator-bump close time that the row exists with at minimum a 'status: open' or 'pending' marker (not a closed marker — the TF must be open at cascade close time, since the Renovate cycle has not yet occurred). The §6 024B acceptance row should add: 'for onboarded-operator-bump: the TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug> STATUS.md row must carry at minimum a status field (open/pending) — a bare prefix row without a status field fails CI.' This enforces that the TF row is meaningful at filing time and cannot be trivially closed without adding evidence of the Renovate cycle. The Threshold A check (at 024G) is separately enforced by the completeness/correctness lenses of the 024G R1+R2 review verifying the Renovate PR URL is populated in the row before signing USER-GATE-E.

findings.title: Pattern scan: other carve-out paths missing both-assertion coverage — onboarded path has no negative assertion, but this is appropriate by design
findings.evidence: The R4 scan checks whether other invariant 2 paths have the same negative-assertion gap. The onboarded path requires log-file modification AND target match — it has no negative assertion (no log-file-absence check). This is correct: the onboarded path asserts the log WAS modified (positive assertion), so there is no negative assertion to add. The bypass risk on this path is a false log entry (wrong target, forged content), not an absent log entry — and that risk is mitigated by the target-match check. The onboarded-operator-bump path requires log-file modification + target match + TF prefix in STATUS.md — the negative assertion gap (R4-NEW-MAJ-002 above) is the TF row content, not the log file. No additional negative-assertion gaps found beyond R4-NEW-MAJ-001 (R-024-06 inconsistency) and R4-NEW-MAJ-002 (TF row content).
findings.outcome: No additional findings beyond R4-NEW-MAJ-001 and R4-NEW-MAJ-002

findings.title: onboarded-operator-bump path requires log-file modification — no bypass via omitting log entry while declaring operator-bump
findings.evidence: Invariant 2, onboarded-operator-bump bullet: 'PR MUST modify docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md (target match as above) AND STATUS.md MUST contain a row matching the standardised prefix TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>.' The log-file modification requirement is present and carries the same target-match check as the onboarded path. A cascade slice cannot declare onboarded-operator-bump and skip the log entry — the CI check requires the log file to be modified. This path does not introduce a new log-file bypass. The bypass surface on this path is limited to the TF row content issue (R4-NEW-MAJ-002).
findings.outcome: No new bypass on log-file requirement for onboarded-operator-bump path

r4_verdict_rationale: R4 verified R3-NEW-MAJ-001 (safety) as CLOSED — all three targeted plan-doc sites (invariant 2, §5.2, §6 024B) correctly specify both the positive assertion (TF reference present) and the negative assertion (log file NOT modified) for the blocked-on-adopter-conflict CI check. R4 then found two new MAJ: (1) R4-NEW-MAJ-001: R-024-06 in the risk table was not updated by fix-round-3 and still describes only the TF-reference-presence check — an authoritative implementation-guidance anchor that instructs Codex executors to implement the pre-fix, bypass-vulnerable specification. (2) R4-NEW-MAJ-002: the onboarded-operator-bump CI check verifies only that STATUS.md contains the standardised prefix string — a stub row (bare prefix slug, no status field, no Renovate PR URL) passes CI; the Threshold A credit mechanism for operator-bump adopters is then entirely reviewer-dependent, with no machine-verifiable evidence that a real Renovate cycle occurred. This is the same negative-assertion gap pattern that FIX-ROUND-3.md's 'Notable lesson' documents as the canonical defect class introduced by carve-out clauses: positive evidence verified (prefix present), absence of contradicting evidence not asserted (meaningful content not required). The R4 fixpoint criterion (0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ on a complete cycle) is not met.
